narrative:
The model determined that you have a 31% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

Three pieces of information about you weighed most heavily in this decision. First, the size of your savings account worked strongly in your favor. Having €1,000 or more saved is relatively rare among approved applicants (only 2.9% of them have this level), and the model viewed this as a clear positive signal of financial responsibility.

Unfortunately, two other factors pulled the prediction in the opposite direction and ultimately outweighed the benefit of your savings. The fact that you are requesting the loan to buy a new car increased the assessed risk, as new-car loans have historically shown higher default rates than loans for other purposes such as home improvements or education. Similarly, the current status of your checking account (between 0 and 200 DM) also raised the predicted risk. While many approved applicants have no checking account at all, those who do maintain small positive balances tend to be viewed as higher risk than those with larger or more stable balances.

Taken together, these last two factors were decisive. To improve your chances next time, consider applying for a smaller loan amount, waiting until your checking account shows a stronger positive balance, or requesting credit for a purpose the bank sees as lower risk. You may also want to review your full credit report before reapplying.
